findings.summary: A crashed or aborted test binary leaves the name list incomplete, so a new failure can still be excused
findings.evidence: Names are recorded whenever the process exits with a code and the command is plain `cargo test`. When a test binary dies from a stack overflow, abort, segfault or `process::exit`, it prints no indented `failures:` list and no `test result:` line. cargo with `--no-fail-fast` goes on to the other binaries and exits 101. Example: the base fails X in binary A; the candidate fails X in A and crashes binary B. The candidate list is {X}, a subset of the base, so `is_pre_existing` returns true and the job's own failure is excused. This is the same masking the plan closed for cargo's early stop (Decision 2), so the claim that the list is complete by construction does not hold. Fix: Check that each binary's output is complete. For every `Running`/`Doc-tests` section, require a `test result:` line whose failed count equals the number of names listed for that binary. If a section ends without one, add a marker name such as `<binary> (did not finish)`. The marker counts as new unless the base has the same marker. The simpler option is to record no names and fall back to the name-level rule. Add a parser fixture for a crashed binary, and a verify test with base {A X} against candidate {A X, B crashed} showing the check is not pre-existing.
findings.location: Decisions 2 and 3; Steps 2 (`failed_test_names`, the records-names rule in `run_check`)

findings.summary: Case (b) in the reading, a clash with a concurrent change, is not separated by this change
findings.evidence: The reading says name-only detection makes (b) a clash with a concurrent change look like the job's own failure. Comparing per test against the job's fixed base only covers (a), a different test failing inside a check that already failed. The plan never says what happens to (b). Fix: State in the change description and the CHANGELOG that this change covers (a) only, and add (b) to the open questions, so the entry does not overclaim.

findings.summary: The recorded command differs from the command that ran
findings.evidence: `run_check` sets `command: spec.run.clone()` (checks.rs:215, 266). After the change the record says `cargo test --locked` while the process actually ran `cargo test --no-fail-fast --locked`. Nothing in the record shows the difference, so someone reading it later is misled. Fix: Keep `command` unchanged so the verifier's command matching still works, but add a short note to the run's `note`, or document on the field, that the flag was added. Or say this in the design doc note.
findings.location: Decision 2 (`--no-fail-fast` inserted in executed args, `command` kept as configured)

summary: The plan fixes the problem where it starts. Today `Baseline::failed_before` (records.rs:2490) and `verify::is_pre_existing` (verify.rs:134) compare checks by name only. The plan records failing test names in one optional `CheckRun` field, filled in `run_check` (checks.rs:190). That one function produces both the base and the candidate runs (`baseline_runs` at checks.rs:286 calls it). Every function and helper the plan names exists where it says. I checked: `check` is at verify.rs:678, `baseline_with` at verify.rs:731, `judge_against` at verify.rs:741 and `sh_spec` at checks.rs:309. I also checked that job runs use `NoCi` (run/mod.rs:1283), so the candidate checks run locally and will record names. CI-reused records will have none. The serde default with skip-if-empty keeps old records parsing under `deny_unknown_fields`. The demonstrations call the real production functions, not test doubles. One soundness gap remains. The plan says `--no-fail-fast` makes the name list "complete by construction", but a test binary that crashes or aborts prints no `failures:` list, while cargo still exits with a code. The candidate list can then still be a subset of the base list, so a new failure the job caused is excused. That is the masking this fix is meant to remove. The fix is a cheap check that cargo's own per-binary output already allows. The other findings are minor or nits. I weighed Athena's eight findings about files outside the deliverables: adding a field forces those one-line edits, and the plan explains why.
